# Tapir commands: MEP Commands / MEP Commands (extended)

The 47 commands of this group, with their parameters, results and examples. Every group and how a command is sent: [commands.md](https://archicad-api.com/commands.md).

## MEP Commands

### GetMEPElements

Retrieves the MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing) elements of the project (every element the MEP API lists, and from Archicad 30 the electrical panels and devices), optionally filtered by type and domain. MEP elements are ordinary elements, so the generic element commands work on them as well (for example they can be deleted with the DeleteElements command). Available from Archicad 28.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.6. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetMEPElements

Parameters:

- `elementTypes` (array of MEPElementType): Optional filter for the MEP element types.
- `domains` (array of MEPDomain): Optional filter for the MEP domains.

Returns:

- `elements` (array of MEPElement, required): The MEP elements.

Grasshopper: `GetMEPElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPElements.py): Lists the duct and pipe routes and terminals of the project with GetMEPElements. Leave out both filters to list every MEP element. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### GetMEPRoutingElements

Retrieves the details of the given MEP routing elements: domain, MEP system, offset from the home story, branch preference table, the ports logically connected at the route's beginning and end, the floor plan display settings (cut plane position, floor plan display option, show projection and on-story visibility, from Archicad 29), route polyline, segments with cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), begin and end nodes, anchor, reference line offsets, wall thickness, flange size, connection style, insulation thickness and rigid segments, and nodes with their incoming and outgoing segments, preferred transition placement, elbows and transitions, and the node positions with the key ModifyMEPRoutingElements writes them with. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.6. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetMEPRoutingElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)

Returns:

- `routingElements` (MEPRoutingElementDetailsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `GetMEPRoutingElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPRoutingElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPRoutingElements.py): Prints the polyline, segments and nodes of the first MEP routes of the project with GetMEPRoutingElements. Needs at least one MEP route (duct, pipe or cable carrier). Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### GetMEPPorts

Retrieves the ports of the given MEP elements including position, shape, size, connection status (Archicad 27: whether the port is connected, from Archicad 28: whether it is physically connected) and connection style (from Archicad 30), the flow direction of piping and ventilation ports (from Archicad 28), the nominal size of piping ports (from Archicad 30), and the outer diameter, wall thickness and flange size (Archicad 30) of piping and ventilation ports. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.6. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetMEPPorts

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)

Returns:

- `elementPorts` (MEPElementPortsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `GetMEPPortsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPPorts.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPPorts.py): Prints the ports of the first MEP elements of the project with GetMEPPorts. Needs at least one MEP element. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### GetMEPDistributionSystems

Retrieves the MEP distribution systems of the project with their domain, MEP system attribute, member elements, physical systems (from Archicad 29) and optionally their tree: the elements from the root element on, each with its previous and next elements and the connecting ports. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.6. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetMEPDistributionSystems

Parameters:

- `includeTree` (boolean): Whether to return the tree of each system: its elements from the root element on, each with the element it is connected to on the way from the root. False when not given.

Returns:

- `distributionSystems` (array of MEPDistributionSystem, required): The distribution systems of the project.
- `ports` (array of Guid): The ports in the distribution systems graph (see GetMEPPorts).

Grasshopper: `GetMEPDistributionSystemsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPDistributionSystems.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPDistributionSystems.py): Prints the MEP distribution systems of the project and their element trees with GetMEPDistributionSystems. The physical systems of a distribution system are returned from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### CreateMEPRoutingElements

Creates MEP routing elements (duct, pipe or cable carrier routes) along the given polylines with optional cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), MEP system and layer (also set on the segments, elbows and transitions), and optional elbow and transition defaults (preference tables and elbow radius factor, from Archicad 29) that apply only to what is placed. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.6. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateMEPRoutingElements

Parameters:

- `routingElementsData` (array of MEPRoutingElementData, required): Array of data to create MEP routing elements.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateMEPRoutingElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/CreateMEPRoutingElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/CreateMEPRoutingElements.py): Creates a rectangular duct route with one corner and a circular pipe route with CreateMEPRoutingElements. Coordinates are in meters. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.6. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateMEPElements

### ModifyMEPRoutingElements

Modifies the given MEP routing elements: MEP system, branch preference table, floor plan display settings (cut plane position, floor plan display option, show projection and on-story visibility, from Archicad 29), cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), anchor, reference line offsets, wall thickness, flange size and connection style of all segments, preferred transition placement of all nodes, insulation thickness of the whole route (segments, elbows and transitions), and node positions. Available from Archicad 28.

Creates a temporary duct route, modifies it, reads it back and deletes it. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### RebuildMEPRoutingElements

Rebuilds the given MEP routing elements along new node coordinates or along their current polyline: this adds or removes nodes (bend points), leaves out with removeCollinearNodes the nodes where the route goes straight on (as Purge Unused MEP Nodes does), and with resetCustomSegments resets customized segments and nodes (as Reset Custom Segments does). Each route is deleted and placed again from its own settings, under its own guid when Archicad allows it and else under a new one, which the response gives. Every segment, node and fitting gets a new guid (see guidMap); labels, dimensions and other things attached to them are not carried over. Use ModifyMEPRoutingElements nodePositions instead when the node count stays the same: it keeps every guid. Kept: each new segment gets the size (shape, width, height, reference id) and the preference table, anchor, reference line offsets, wall thickness, connection style, flange size and rigid segment settings (insulation) of the old segment it lies along most, and each new node the transition placement and elbow and transition settings of the old node at its position (a new segment along old segments of different sizes gets those of the one it overlaps most, with a warning; a segment along no old segment, such as a new end, those of its nearest neighbour along the route); the route's layer, home story, renovation status (given to every part), element ID, classifications and the property values set on it; and its connections at both ends. Not kept: the guids of the segments, rigid segments, nodes, elbows and transitions; the element IDs, classifications, property values and own renovation status of single parts; and the route's design option, which is not set. Refused, with nothing changed: a route that ends at a tee (Branch) or has a take-off on a segment, which Archicad deletes with the route. What could not be carried over is listed in the item's warnings. Nothing is changed when the nodes make a segment without length or the route cannot be deleted. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RebuildMEPRoutingElements

Parameters:

- `routingElements` (array of object, required): The routing elements to rebuild. Each is deleted and placed again. Every segment, node and fitting gets a new guid (see guidMap); labels, dimensions and other things attached to them are not carried over. Use ModifyMEPRoutingElements nodePositions instead when the node count stays the same: it keeps every guid.
  - `routingElementId` (ElementId, required): The routing element (duct, pipe or cable carrier route) to rebuild.
  - `nodeCoordinates` (array of Coordinate3D): The new corner points of the route, at least 2, absolute like the polyline GetMEPRoutingElements returns. Fewer or more points than the route has nodes remove or add nodes. Omitted: the route's current polyline.
  - `removeCollinearNodes` (boolean): Leaves out every inner node that lies on the straight line between its neighbours (within 1 mm), as Purge Unused MEP Nodes does, and every node on top of the previous one. Default false.
  - `resetCustomSegments` (boolean): True gives every segment and node the route's uncustomized settings, as Reset Custom Segments does. False (default) gives each new segment the size and settings of the old segment it lies along most (within 1 mm), and each new node those of the old node at its position; a segment along no old segment takes the settings of its nearest neighbour along the route (the one before it first), and nodes without an old counterpart take the route's uncustomized settings.

Returns:

- `elements` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): One item for each given routing element, in order.

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/RebuildMEPRoutingElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/RebuildMEPRoutingElements.py): Adds a node to a pipe route, then leaves out a node where it goes straight on, with RebuildMEPRoutingElements. Creates a temporary pipe route, rebuilds it twice, reads it back and deletes it. Requires Archicad 28 or later. Every segment, node and fitting gets a new guid (see guidMap in the response); labels, dimensions and other things attached to them are not carried over. Use ModifyMEPRoutingElements nodePositions instead when the node count stays the same: it keeps every guid. The route keeps its guid when Archicad allows it (else the response gives the new one), and each new segment keeps the size and settings of the old segment it lies along. Not kept: the element IDs, classifications, property values and own renovation status of single parts, and the route's design option; the item's warnings list anything else not carried over. A route that ends at a tee or has a take-off is refused, since Archicad deletes those with the route.

### ModifyMEPPorts

Modifies the given MEP ports (as returned by GetMEPPorts): shape, width, height (not of piping ports), connection style (from Archicad 30), the flow direction of piping and ventilation ports, and the outer diameter and nominal size (from Archicad 30) of piping ports. Only the given fields are changed. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyMEPPorts

Parameters:

- `portsData` (array of MEPPortModificationData, required): Array of data to modify MEP ports. Only provided fields are changed.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `ModifyMEPPortsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/ModifyMEPPorts.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/ModifyMEPPorts.py): Changes MEP ports with ModifyMEPPorts: the flow direction and outer diameter of a piping terminal's port, and the connection size (width and height) of an air terminal. Creates a temporary piping terminal and a ventilation terminal, modifies their ports, reads them back and deletes them. GetMEPPorts reads the ports of MEP elements such as terminals, not of routes. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### ConnectMEPElements

Connects MEP routing elements to other MEP elements or routes. Merges routes, splits routes or creates branch elements as needed. The first or last node of the 'connectToId' route must lie exactly on the 'routingElementId' route, so for a tee pass the main route as 'routingElementId' and the branch as 'connectToId'. A failed connection says which condition is not met. Archicad 27 does not report the merged, split or created elements. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.6. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ConnectMEPElements

Parameters:

- `connectionsData` (array of MEPConnectionData, required): Array of connections to create.

Returns:

- `connectionResults` (MEPConnectionResultsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `ConnectMEPElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/ConnectMEPElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/ConnectMEPElements.py): Connects a branch duct to the middle of a main duct with ConnectMEPElements, which creates a branch element. Creates the two duct routes; the branch starts on the main route, as the command needs. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### GetMEPPreferenceTables

Gets the circular cross section preference tables (referenceId, diameter, wall thickness, description) and the reference set of the Piping or Ventilation domain, optionally with the elbow, branch and transition preference tables, plus the rectangular duct tables of the Ventilation domain or the segment tables of the CableCarrier domain. Each table has its name and whether it is editable; the segment tables also have their segmentation lengths from Archicad 29. The rows of the circular, elbow, branch and transition tables say whether they are valid, and the reference set and the angle set say which of their reference ids and angles are defined. The angle set and the transition tables are available from Archicad 29. Every row has its index in the table, as ModifyMEPPreferenceTables expects it. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetMEPPreferenceTables

Parameters:

- `domain` (MEPPreferenceTableDomain, required): The MEP domain of the segment preference tables.
- `includeFittingTables` (boolean): Also return the elbow, branch and transition preference tables. Defaults to false. Ignored for the CableCarrier domain.

Returns:

- `tables` (array of MEPPreferenceTable, required): The circular segment preference tables of the domain. Empty for the CableCarrier domain.
- `rectangularTables` (array of MEPValuePreferenceTable): The rectangular segment preference tables of the Ventilation domain.
- `cableCarrierTables` (array of MEPValuePreferenceTable): The segment preference tables of the CableCarrier domain.
- `referenceSet` (MEPReferenceSet): The reference set of the Piping or Ventilation domain. Not returned for the CableCarrier domain.
- `angleSet` (MEPAngleSet): Available from Archicad 29.
- `elbowTables` (array of MEPElbowPreferenceTable): The elbow preference tables of the domain. Only when includeFittingTables is true.
- `branchTables` (array of MEPBranchPreferenceTable): The branch preference tables of the domain. Only when includeFittingTables is true.
- `transitionTables` (array of MEPTransitionPreferenceTable): The transition preference tables of the domain. Only when includeFittingTables is true, available from Archicad 29.

Grasshopper: `GetMEPPreferenceTablesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPPreferenceTables.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPPreferenceTables.py): Prints the pipe preference tables of the project, with the elbow, branch and transition tables, using GetMEPPreferenceTables. The angle set and the transition tables are returned from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### ModifyMEPPreferenceTables

Modifies the MEP preference tables of a domain, in the shape GetMEPPreferenceTables returns them: adds tables, changes their names, segmentation lengths (from Archicad 29) and row values and descriptions, deletes or empties rows, adds rows to the rectangular duct and cable carrier tables, deletes tables, deletes reference ids from the reference set, and adds and deletes angles of the angle set (from Archicad 29). Each table is changed in one undoable step. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyMEPPreferenceTables

Parameters:

- `domain` (MEPPreferenceTableDomain, required): The MEP domain of the segment preference tables.
- `tablesToAdd` (array of MEPPreferenceTableAddition): New tables to add to the domain, before the other changes.
- `tables` (array of MEPPreferenceTableChange): The tables of the domain to change, in the shape GetMEPPreferenceTables returns them. Each table is changed in one undoable step.
- `tablesToDelete` (array of string): The guids of the tables of the domain to delete, after the other table changes.
- `referenceIdsToDelete` (array of integer): Reference ids to delete from the reference set of the Piping or Ventilation domain.
- `anglesToAdd` (array of number): Angles in degrees, between 1 and 90, to add to the angle set of the Piping or Ventilation domain, so that elbow and branch rows can have them. They are added before the tables are changed. Available from Archicad 29.
- `anglesToDelete` (array of number): Angles to delete from the angle set of the Piping or Ventilation domain, as GetMEPPreferenceTables returns them. Available from Archicad 29.

Returns:

- `addedTables` (array of object or FailedExecutionResult, required): One item for each item of tablesToAdd: the guid of the new table, or the error.
- `tables` (ExecutionResults, required): One result for each item of tables.
- `deletedTables` (ExecutionResults, required): One result for each item of tablesToDelete.
- `referenceSet` (ExecutionResult): Only when referenceIdsToDelete is given.
- `addedAngles` (ExecutionResult): Only when anglesToAdd is given.
- `angleSet` (ExecutionResult): Only when anglesToDelete is given.

Grasshopper: `ModifyMEPPreferenceTablesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/ModifyMEPPreferenceTables.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/ModifyMEPPreferenceTables.py): Adds a cable carrier segment table, renames it and fills it with rows using ModifyMEPPreferenceTables, then deletes it. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### GetMEPToolDefaults

Retrieves the current settings of the MEP tools per domain, without changing them: the routing tool (MEP system, branch preference table, floor plan display settings from Archicad 29, and its segment, node, elbow (Archicad 27 and from Archicad 29) and transition defaults), its rigid segment and branch defaults, the flexible segment tool, the library part, insulation and port settings of the terminal, accessory, fitting and equipment tools, and from Archicad 30 the electrical panel tool with its number of circuit defaults. Archicad 27 gives fewer settings, and only the shape of the ports. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetMEPToolDefaults

Parameters:

- `domains` (array of MEPDomain): The domains to return the tool defaults of. All three when not given.

Returns:

- `toolDefaults` (array of MEPDomainToolDefaults, required): The tool defaults of each requested domain, in the order requested.
- `equipment` (MEPElementDefaultDetails): The default of the Equipment tool, which has no domain. Left out when Archicad gives none.
- `electricalPanel` (ElectricalPanelToolDefaults)

Grasshopper: `GetMEPToolDefaultsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPToolDefaults.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPToolDefaults.py): Prints the current settings of the ventilation and piping MEP tools with GetMEPToolDefaults. Leave out 'domains' to get all three domains. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### TransferMEPSettings

Picks up the settings of an MEP element and injects them into other MEP elements of the same type and domain, like Archicad's pick up and inject parameters. Works for routing elements, terminals, accessories, equipment, fittings, flexible segments, branches, take-offs and (from Archicad 30) electrical panels and devices. Each target is changed in its own undoable step. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#TransferMEPSettings

Parameters:

- `sourceElementId` (ElementId, required): The MEP element to pick up the settings from: a routing element, terminal, accessory, equipment, fitting, flexible segment, branch, take-off, or (from Archicad 30) electrical panel or device.
- `targetElements` (Elements, required): The MEP elements to inject the settings into. Each must be of the type and domain of the source element.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `TransferMEPSettingsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/TransferMEPSettings.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/TransferMEPSettings.py): Copies the settings of a wide duct route onto a narrow one with TransferMEPSettings. Creates two temporary duct routes, transfers the settings, reads the target back and deletes both. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### GetMEPPhysicalSystemsOfElements

Returns the physical systems each of the given MEP elements is part of. Available from Archicad 29.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetMEPPhysicalSystemsOfElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)

Returns:

- `physicalSystemsOfElements` (array of MEPPhysicalSystemsOfElement, required): The physical systems of each given element, in the order of the elements.

Grasshopper: `GetMEPPhysicalSystemsOfElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPPhysicalSystemsOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPPhysicalSystemsOfElements.py): Prints the physical systems the first MEP elements of the project belong to with GetMEPPhysicalSystemsOfElements. Needs at least one MEP element. Requires Archicad 29 or later.

### CreateMEPFlexibleSegments

Creates MEP flexible segments through the given control points, or along a polyline of alternating line and spline parts (Piping), with the current settings of the Flexible Segment tool of their domain, optionally with the orientation (control points) or direction (polyline) at both ends. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateMEPFlexibleSegments

Parameters:

- `flexibleSegmentsData` (array of MEPFlexibleSegmentCreationData, required): Array of data to place MEP flexible segments with the current settings of the Flexible Segment tool of their domain (see GetMEPToolDefaults).

Grasshopper: `CreateMEPFlexibleSegmentsComponent`

Uses the current settings of the Flexible Segment tool. Coordinates are in meters. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### CreateMEPTakeOffs

Creates MEP take-offs on the given routing segments, at a distance from the beginning of the segment (not more than its length) and optionally rotated around its axis by a multiple of 90 degrees, with the current settings of the Take-Off tool of their domain (by default the domain of the segment's routing element), optionally with their length and without insulation, which apply only to what is created. Archicad only has Ventilation take-offs. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateMEPTakeOffs

Parameters:

- `takeOffsData` (array of MEPTakeOffCreationData, required): Array of data to create MEP take-offs on routing segments with the current settings of the Take-Off tool of their domain.

Grasshopper: `CreateMEPTakeOffsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/CreateMEPTakeOffs.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/CreateMEPTakeOffs.py): Creates a take-off 2 m from the start of a new duct route with CreateMEPTakeOffs. Creates the duct route first; the take-off uses the current settings of the Take-Off tool of the route's domain (no 'domain' given), faces up (a quarter turn) and has no insulation. Archicad only has Ventilation take-offs. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### ModifyMEPElements

Modifies placed MEP elements: the anchor point, orientation and library part of terminals, accessories, equipment, fittings and flexible segments, their size along the local x and y axes (from Archicad 30), the control points, polyline (Piping, from Archicad 28), and width and height of flexible segments. Only the given fields are changed, in one undo step with one execution result per element; an item with a field that does not fit its element changes nothing. Archicad reports a 'libraryPartId' it does not find, or a library part that keeps its own size, only after the item's other changes were made, so that item's error says which changes stayed. The size of the connections is set with ModifyMEPPorts. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyMEPElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (array of MEPElementModificationData, required): The MEP elements to modify, each with the fields to change. Only the given fields are changed.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `ModifyMEPElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/ModifyMEPElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/ModifyMEPElements.py): Requires Archicad 27 or newer. On Archicad 27 this example reads the tool defaults and works on the selected MEP elements (select a flexible segment and a terminal first), because Archicad 27 has no commands to place them. From Archicad 28 it places its own elements and deletes them at the end.

### GetMEPRoutingParameters

Gets the routing parameters of placed MEP elements: of a routing element its routing node parameters (preferred transition placement, elbow from Archicad 29, transition) and routing segment parameters (cross section, preference table, anchor, reference line offsets, wall thickness, flange size, connection style); of a routing node its elbow (from Archicad 29) and transition parameters; of a routing segment its rigid segment parameters (Archicad 28 only). Available from Archicad 28.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetMEPRoutingParameters

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required): MEP routing elements, routing nodes or routing segments.

Needs at least one MEP route. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### SetMEPRoutingParameters

Sets the routing parameters of placed MEP elements: the routing segment parameters (cross section and preference table) and, from Archicad 29, the routing node parameters (elbow radius factor and preference table, transition preference table) of routing elements, and the elbow and transition parameters of routing nodes (from Archicad 29). Only the given keys are changed, with one execution result per element. A changed preference table is also set on each of the route's segments and nodes and injected into them, because Archicad 29 can otherwise keep the old one; the item fails if they still report the old table. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: MEP Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetMEPRoutingParameters

Parameters:

- `elements` (array of ElementMEPRoutingParameters, required): The routing parameters to change. Only the given keys are changed. An item gives either routingNodeParameters and/or routingSegmentParameters for a routing element, or elbowParameters and/or transitionParameters for a routing node.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `SetMEPRoutingParametersComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/SetMEPRoutingParameters.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/SetMEPRoutingParameters.py): Makes a pipe route circular and changes the elbow radius factor of its nodes with SetMEPRoutingParameters. Creates a temporary pipe route with one corner, changes it, reads the parameters back and deletes it. The elbow parameters can be set from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

## MEP Commands (extended)

### GetMEPPreferenceTableRows

Gets rows of a segment, branch, elbow or (from Archicad 29) transition preference table by their key (the reference ids and, for branch and elbow rows from Archicad 29, the angle): whether the row is valid and its values (diameters, wall thickness, radius, length, angle, branch offset, connection length, description), and whether the table exists. Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables only give whether they exist, as their rows have no key. On Archicad 27, which has one kind of preference table, a row is found by its shape and index and has a value and a description; the table's name and number of rows per shape are returned too. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: MEP Commands (extended). Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetMEPPreferenceTableRows

Parameters:

- `tableId` (MEPPreferenceTableId, required): The guid of a preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables (the branch, elbow and transition tables with includeFittingTables): a pipe or circular duct segment table, a branch or elbow table of the Piping or Ventilation domain, or, from Archicad 29, a transition table. Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables are found too, but their rows have no key. Archicad 27: any preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers.
- `keys` (array of MEPPreferenceRowKey, required): The keys of the rows to get.

Returns:

- `exists` (boolean, required): Whether the table exists.
- `name` (string): Archicad 27 only: the name of the table.
- `sizes` (object): Archicad 27 only: the number of rows of each shape.
  - `Circular` (integer)
  - `Rectangular` (integer)
- `rows` (array of MEPPreferenceRowDetails or ErrorItem, required): The rows in the order of the keys.

Grasshopper: `GetMEPPreferenceTableRowsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPPreferenceTableRows.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPPreferenceTableRows.py): Reads the first two rows of the first pipe segment preference table by their reference id with GetMEPPreferenceTableRows. Requires Archicad 28 or later (on Archicad 27 the keys are a shape and an index).

### SetMEPPreferenceTableRows

Sets the given values of rows of a segment, branch, elbow or (from Archicad 29) transition preference table, found by their key (the reference ids and, for branch and elbow rows from Archicad 29, the angle). Only the given values are changed, in one undo step. On Archicad 27 a row is found by its shape and index, its value and description are set, and its index after the call is returned; the keys give the indices before the call. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: MEP Commands (extended). Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetMEPPreferenceTableRows

Parameters:

- `tableId` (MEPPreferenceTableId, required): The guid of a preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables (the branch, elbow and transition tables with includeFittingTables): a pipe or circular duct segment table, a branch or elbow table of the Piping or Ventilation domain, or, from Archicad 29, a transition table. Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables are found too, but their rows have no key. Archicad 27: any preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers.
- `rows` (array of MEPPreferenceRowUpdate, required): The rows to change. Only the given values are set.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (array of MEPPreferenceRowUpdateResult or FailedExecutionResult, required): One result per row, in the order of the rows.

Grasshopper: `SetMEPPreferenceTableRowsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/SetMEPPreferenceTableRows.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/SetMEPPreferenceTableRows.py): Changes the description of a row of an editable pipe segment preference table with SetMEPPreferenceTableRows. Reads the row, changes it, reads it back and restores the old description. Requires Archicad 28 or later (on Archicad 27 the key is a shape and an index).

### AddMEPPreferenceTableRows

Adds rows with the given keys and optionally values to a branch, elbow or transition preference table and returns their index, in one undo step. Branch tables from Archicad 28, elbow and transition tables from Archicad 29; segment tables have a row for each reference id. On Archicad 27 a row is added to the list of the given shape of any preference table, and the index of each new row after the call is returned. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: MEP Commands (extended). Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#AddMEPPreferenceTableRows

Parameters:

- `tableId` (MEPPreferenceTableId, required): The guid of a preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables (the branch, elbow and transition tables with includeFittingTables): a pipe or circular duct segment table, a branch or elbow table of the Piping or Ventilation domain, or, from Archicad 29, a transition table. Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables are found too, but their rows have no key. Archicad 27: any preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers.
- `rows` (array of MEPPreferenceRowAddition, required): The rows to add, with their key and optionally their values. Branch tables from Archicad 28, elbow and transition tables from Archicad 29. Segment tables have a row for each reference id, so no row can be added to them. Archicad 27: the key has the shape only, the table gives the index.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (array of MEPPreferenceRowAdditionResult or FailedExecutionResult, required): One result per row, in the order of the rows.

Grasshopper: `AddMEPPreferenceTableRowsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/AddMEPPreferenceTableRows.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/AddMEPPreferenceTableRows.py): Adds a row to the first editable pipe elbow preference table with AddMEPPreferenceTableRows. The new row gets the reference id of the first row and an angle of the angle set that this reference id has no row for yet; it is deleted again at the end. Elbow rows can be added from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 29 or later.

### DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows

Deletes rows of a segment, branch, elbow or (from Archicad 29) transition preference table by their key (the reference ids and, for branch and elbow rows from Archicad 29, the angle), in one undo step. The rows of segment tables, and of the elbow tables of Archicad 28, are emptied instead. On Archicad 27 a row is found by its shape and index. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: MEP Commands (extended). Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows

Parameters:

- `tableId` (MEPPreferenceTableId, required): The guid of a preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables (the branch, elbow and transition tables with includeFittingTables): a pipe or circular duct segment table, a branch or elbow table of the Piping or Ventilation domain, or, from Archicad 29, a transition table. Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables are found too, but their rows have no key. Archicad 27: any preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers.
- `keys` (array of MEPPreferenceRowKey, required): The keys of the rows to delete. Segment tables, and the elbow tables of Archicad 28, have a row for each reference id, which is emptied instead. Archicad 27: the indices are those before the call; the rows are deleted from the highest index down.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRowsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows.py): Adds a row to the first editable pipe elbow preference table and deletes it again with DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows. The row gets the reference id of the first row and an angle of the angle set that this reference id has no row for yet. Rows of segment tables are emptied instead of deleted. Requires Archicad 29 or later.

### GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers

Lists the preference tables of the Piping, Ventilation and Cable Carrier preference table containers of Archicad 27: their id, name, whether they exist and their number of rows per shape, and whether the container exists. Only for Archicad 27; from Archicad 28 use GetMEPPreferenceTables.

Group: MEP Commands (extended). Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers

Parameters:

- `domains` (array of MEPPreferenceTableDomain): The domains whose preference tables to list. Defaults to all three.

Returns:

- `containers` (array of MEPPreferenceTableContainer or ErrorItem, required): The preference table container of each domain, in the order of the domains.

Grasshopper: `GetMEPPreferenceTableContainersComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers.py): Lists the preference tables of the pipe and duct preference table containers with GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers. Only for Archicad 27; from Archicad 28 use GetMEPPreferenceTables.

### CreateMEPPreferenceTables

Adds empty preference tables with the given names to the preference table container of a domain of Archicad 27 and returns their id, in one undo step. Only for Archicad 27.

Group: MEP Commands (extended). Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateMEPPreferenceTables

Parameters:

- `domain` (MEPPreferenceTableDomain, required): The MEP domain of a preference table container.
- `tables` (array of object, required): The tables to add, empty, to the preference table container of the domain.
  - `name` (string, required)

Returns:

- `executionResults` (array of MEPPreferenceTableCreationResult or FailedExecutionResult, required): One result per table, in the order of the tables.

Grasshopper: `CreateMEPPreferenceTablesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/CreateMEPPreferenceTables.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/MEP/CreateMEPPreferenceTables.py): Adds an empty pipe preference table named "Tapir example" with CreateMEPPreferenceTables. Every run adds a new table. Only for Archicad 27; from Archicad 28 use ModifyMEPPreferenceTables.

## Shared schema definitions

Types that parameters and results refer to by name.

### Elements

array of ElementIdArrayItem: A list of elements.

### ElementIdArrayItem

object
- `elementId` (ElementId, required)

### ElementIdOrError

ElementIdArrayItem or ErrorItem: An element identifier or an error.

### ElementIdsOrErrors

array of ElementIdOrError: A list of element identifiers or errors.

### MEPRoutingSegmentDetails

object: The details of an MEP routing segment.
- `elementId` (ElementId, required)
- `routingElementId` (ElementId): The routing element the segment belongs to.
- `crossSectionWidth` (number, required)
- `crossSectionHeight` (number, required)
- `crossSectionShape` (string, required)
- `crossSectionReferenceId` (integer): The cross section reference id of the segment in its preference table (meaningful for circular cross sections).
- `preferenceTableId` (Guid): The guid of the segment preference table used by the segment (see GetMEPPreferenceTables).
- `beginNodeId` (ElementId): The routing node at the beginning of the segment.
- `endNodeId` (ElementId): The routing node at the end of the segment.
- `anchor` (MEPRoutingAnchor)
- `referenceLineOffsetX` (number): The horizontal offset of the reference line from the anchor point.
- `referenceLineOffsetY` (number): The vertical offset of the reference line from the anchor point.
- `wallThickness` (number): The wall thickness of the segment.
- `flangeSize` (number): The flange size of the segment (width for Ventilation, diameter for Piping). It is used only when the connection style is Flanged; Archicad 29 also returns it for other styles.
- `insulationThickness` (number): The insulation thickness of the rigid segments of the segment. Only present when they are insulated (never for cable carriers).
- `connectionStyle` (MEPConnectionStyle)
- `rigidSegments` (Elements): The rigid segments (the straight duct, pipe or cable carrier pieces) of the routing segment.

### MEPRoutingNodeDetails

object: The details of an MEP routing node.
- `elementId` (ElementId, required)
- `routingElementId` (ElementId): The routing element the node belongs to.
- `position` (Coordinate3D, required)
- `incomingSegmentId` (ElementId): The routing segment ending at this node. Not present at the beginning of the route.
- `outgoingSegmentId` (ElementId): The routing segment starting at this node. Not present at the end of the route.
- `preferredTransitionPlacement` (MEPPreferredTransitionPlacement)
- `elbows` (Elements): The elbows (bends in Archicad 28) at this node.
- `transitions` (Elements): The transitions at this node.

### MEPRoutingElementDetails

object: The details of an MEP routing element.
- `domain` (MEPDomainOrUnknown, required)
- `mepSystemId` (AttributeId, required)
- `floorIndex` (integer): The index of the home story of the routing element (see GetStories).
- `offsetFromHomeStory` (number): The offset of the lowest node of the routing element from the level of its home story.
- `branchPreferenceTableId` (Guid): The guid of the branch preference table used by the routing element (see GetMEPPreferenceTables). Not present when the routing element has none.
- `logicallyConnectedPortIdAtRouteBegin` (Guid): The port logically connected to the beginning of the route (see GetMEPPorts). Not present when nothing is connected there.
- `logicallyConnectedPortIdAtRouteEnd` (Guid): The port logically connected to the end of the route (see GetMEPPorts). Not present when nothing is connected there.
- `cutPlanePosition` (MEPCutPlanePosition)
- `floorPlanDisplayOption` (MEPFloorPlanDisplayOption)
- `showProjection` (MEPShowProjection)
- `onStoryVisibility` (MEPOnStoryVisibility)
- `polyline` (array of Coordinate3D, required)
- `segments` (array of MEPRoutingSegmentDetails, required)
- `nodes` (array of MEPRoutingNodeDetails, required)
- `nodePositions` (array of Coordinate3D): The position of every node, in the order of nodes: the key ModifyMEPRoutingElements writes the node positions with, so they can be sent back. The other settings ModifyMEPRoutingElements applies to all segments or all nodes are read per segment (segments) and per node (nodes), with the same keys.

### MEPRoutingElementDetailsOrError

MEPRoutingElementDetails or ErrorItem: The details of an MEP routing element or an error.

### MEPRoutingElementDetailsOrErrors

array of MEPRoutingElementDetailsOrError: A list of MEP routing element details or errors.

### MEPPortDetails

object: The details of a port of an MEP element.
- `portId` (Guid, required)
- `mepElementId` (ElementId): The MEP element the port belongs to.
- `name` (string, required)
- `position` (Coordinate3D, required)
- `direction` (Coordinate3D, required)
- `shape` (string, required)
- `width` (number, required)
- `height` (number, required)
- `domain` (MEPDomainOrUnknown, required)
- `mepSystemId` (AttributeId, required)
- `isPhysicallyConnected` (boolean): Whether the port is physically connected to another port. Available from Archicad 28.
- `isConnected` (boolean): Whether the port is connected to another port. Archicad 27 only; from Archicad 28 see isPhysicallyConnected.
- `connectionStyle` (MEPConnectionStyle): The connection style of the port. Available from Archicad 30.
- `flowDirection` (MEPFlowDirection): The flow direction of a piping or ventilation port.
- `nominalSize` (string): The nominal size of a piping port. Available from Archicad 30.
- `outerDiameter` (number): The outer diameter of a piping port.
- `wallThickness` (number): The wall thickness of a piping or ventilation port.
- `flangeSize` (number): The flange size of a piping or ventilation port. Available from Archicad 30.
- `connectedPortId` (Guid)
- `connectedElementId` (ElementId)

### MEPElementPorts

object: The ports of an MEP element.
- `ports` (array of MEPPortDetails, required)

### MEPElementPortsOrError

MEPElementPorts or ErrorItem: The ports of an MEP element or an error.

### MEPElementPortsOrErrors

array of MEPElementPortsOrError: A list of MEP element ports or errors.

### MEPFlexibleSegmentPolyline

array of object: The geometry of a polyline MEP flexible segment: its line and spline parts in order, which alternate and connect at their ends. Available from Archicad 28.

### MEPConnectionResult

object: The result of connecting an MEP routing element: the routing element deleted by merging, the routing element created by splitting and the branch element created by the connection. Empty in Archicad 27, which does not report them.
- `deletedRoutingElementId` (ElementId)
- `splitRoutingElementId` (ElementId)
- `createdBranchId` (ElementId)

### MEPConnectionResultOrError

MEPConnectionResult or ErrorItem: The result of an MEP connection or an error.

### MEPConnectionResultsOrErrors

array of MEPConnectionResultOrError: A list of MEP connection results or errors.

### ElementId

object: The identifier of an element.
- `guid` (Guid, required)

### AttributeId

object: The identifier of an attribute.
- `guid` (Guid, required)

### Guid

string: A Globally Unique Identifier (or Universally Unique Identifier) in its string representation as defined in RFC 4122.

### Coordinate3D

object: 3D coordinate.
- `x` (number, required): X value of the coordinate.
- `y` (number, required): Y value of the coordinate.
- `z` (number, required): Z value of the coordinate.

### Error

object: The details of an error.
- `code` (integer, required): The code of the error.
- `message` (string, required): The error message.

### ErrorItem

object
- `error` (Error, required)

### SuccessfulExecutionResult

object: The result of a successful execution.
- `success` (boolean (true), required)

### FailedExecutionResult

object: The result of a failed execution.
- `success` (boolean (false), required)
- `error` (Error, required)

### ExecutionResult

SuccessfulExecutionResult or FailedExecutionResult: The result of the execution.

### ExecutionResults

array of ExecutionResult: A list of execution results.

### MEPDomain

string ("Ventilation", "Piping", "CableCarrier"): The MEP domain.

### MEPDomainOrUnknown

string ("Ventilation", "Piping", "CableCarrier", "Unknown"): The reported MEP domain. Unknown indicates that the domain could not be determined.

### MEPElementType

string ("RoutingElement", "RigidSegment", "Elbow", "Transition", "Branch", "Terminal", "Accessory", "Equipment", "Fitting", "FlexibleSegment", "TakeOff", "ElectricalPanel", ...)

### MEPCrossSectionShape

string ("Rectangular", "Circular", "Oval", "UShape"): Shape of an MEP routing segment's cross section or of an MEP port.

### MEPConnectionStyle

string ("SimpleBody", "Flanged", "Welded"): How the pieces of an MEP routing segment, or an MEP port, are connected. For pipes, the settings dialog of Archicad 29 shows SimpleBody as Welded, and Welded is refused on a pipe route.

### MEPFlowDirection

string ("FlowNotDefined", "FlowIn", "FlowOut"): The flow direction of a piping or ventilation port.

### MEPPreferredTransitionPlacement

string ("SmallToLarge", "LargeToSmall"): Where an MEP routing node places its transitions.

### MEPCutPlanePosition

string ("AtUpperDisplayLimit", "ByViewSettings"): Where the floor plan cut plane of an MEP routing element is. Available from Archicad 29.

### MEPFloorPlanDisplayOption

string ("Projected", "ProjectedWithOverhead", "Symbolic", "ByMVO"): How an MEP routing element is shown on the floor plan. Available from Archicad 29.

### MEPShowProjection

string ("ToFloorPlanRange", "ToAbsoluteDisplayLimit", "EntireElement"): How much of an MEP routing element's projection is shown on the floor plan. Available from Archicad 29.

### MEPOnStoryVisibility

string ("AllRelevantStories", "HomeStoryOnly"): On which stories an MEP routing element is shown. Available from Archicad 29.

### MEPPortDefaultDetails

object: The settings of one port of an MEP tool default. Each field is present only where the port's domain and the Archicad version have it: Archicad 27 gives only the index and the shape.
- `index` (integer, required): The index of the port in the default.
- `domain` (MEPDomain)
- `name` (string)
- `shape` (MEPCrossSectionShape)
- `width` (number)
- `height` (number): The height of a ventilation or cable carrier port.
- `diameter` (number): The diameter of a piping port.
- `wallThickness` (number): The wall thickness of a piping or ventilation port.
- `flowDirection` (MEPFlowDirection): The flow direction of a piping or ventilation port.
- `flangeSize` (number): The flange size of a piping or ventilation port, when it has flanges. Available from Archicad 30.
- `connectionStyle` (MEPConnectionStyle): Available from Archicad 30.
- `mepSystemId` (AttributeId)

### MEPElementDefaultDetails

object: The settings of a terminal, accessory, fitting, equipment or branch tool default.
- `libraryPartId` (LibPartUnId, required): The library part the tool places.
- `insulationThickness` (number): The insulation thickness, when the default has insulation.
- `ports` (array of MEPPortDefaultDetails, required)

### MEPDomainToolDefaults

object: The current settings of the MEP tools of one domain. A tool whose default Archicad does not give for the domain is left out; a setting is left out where the Archicad version does not have it.
- `domain` (MEPDomain, required)
- `routingElement` (object): The routing tool default.
  - `mepSystemId` (AttributeId, required)
  - `branchPreferenceTableId` (Guid)
  - `cutPlanePosition` (MEPCutPlanePosition)
  - `floorPlanDisplayOption` (MEPFloorPlanDisplayOption)
  - `showProjection` (MEPShowProjection)
  - `onStoryVisibility` (MEPOnStoryVisibility)
  - `routingSegment` (object, required): The segment default of the routing tool.
  - `routingNode` (object, required): The node default of the routing tool.
- `rigidSegment` (object): The rigid segment default of the routing tool.
  - `shape` (MEPCrossSectionShape): Archicad 27 only. Later versions give the size in routingElement.routingSegment.
  - `width` (number): Archicad 27 only. Later versions give the size in routingElement.routingSegment.
  - `height` (number): Archicad 27 only. Later versions give the size in routingElement.routingSegment.
  - `insulationThickness` (number): The insulation thickness, when the default has insulation.
- `branch` (MEPElementDefaultDetails): The branch default of the routing tool.
- `flexibleSegment` (object): The flexible segment tool default. Archicad 27 has it in the Ventilation domain only.
  - `shape` (MEPCrossSectionShape, required)
  - `width` (number, required)
  - `height` (number, required)
- `terminal` (MEPElementDefaultDetails)
- `accessory` (MEPElementDefaultDetails)
- `fitting` (MEPElementDefaultDetails)

### MEPPreferenceTableDomain

string ("Piping", "Ventilation", "CableCarrier")

### MEPPreferenceRowIndex

integer: The position of the row in its preference table, as ModifyMEPPreferenceTables expects it. Rows that cannot be read are left out of GetMEPPreferenceTables, so this is not always the position in the rows list.

### MEPPreferenceTableType

string ("Segment", "Elbow", "Branch", "Transition"): The kind of preference table container: the segment tables (circular and rectangular ducts share one container), or the elbow, branch or transition tables. CableCarrier has only segment tables, transition tables are available from Archicad 29.

### MEPPreferenceRowChange

object: Changes one row of a preference table, in the shape GetMEPPreferenceTables returns. Only the given values are changed. A value that does not belong to the kind of table is an error; the read-only values (reference ids, branchAxisAngle, isValid, and angle of an elbow table) are ignored.
- `index` (MEPPreferenceRowIndex, required)
- `delete` (boolean): Deletes the row. The circular segment tables, and the elbow tables in Archicad 28, have a fixed row for each reference id; there the row is emptied instead. Cannot be combined with new values.
- `diameter` (number): Circular segment and elbow tables.
- `wallThickness` (number): Circular segment tables.
- `value` (number): Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables. These tables keep their rows ordered by value, so a changed value can move the row; the indices of the other rows given in the same call are followed.
- `radius` (number): Elbow tables.
- `mainAxisDiameter` (number): Branch tables.
- `branchAxisDiameter` (number): Branch tables.
- `length` (number): Branch tables and piping transition tables.
- `branchOffset` (number): Branch tables.
- `connectionLength` (number): Branch tables.
- `beginDiameter` (number): Transition tables.
- `endDiameter` (number): Transition tables.
- `angle` (number): Ventilation transition tables, in the unit GetMEPPreferenceTables returns it. Read-only (ignored) in elbow tables.
- `description` (string)
- `referenceId` (integer): Read-only, ignored.
- `mainAxisReferenceId` (integer): Read-only, ignored.
- `branchAxisReferenceId` (integer): Read-only, ignored.
- `beginReferenceId` (integer): Read-only, ignored.
- `endReferenceId` (integer): Read-only, ignored.
- `branchAxisAngle` (number): Read-only, ignored.
- `isValid` (boolean): Read-only, ignored.

### MEPPreferenceTableChange

object: Changes one preference table, in the shape GetMEPPreferenceTables returns. Only the given values and rows are changed.
- `guid` (string, required): The guid of the table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables.
- `name` (string): The new name of the table.
- `isEditable` (boolean): Read-only, ignored.
- `useIndividualSegmentLengths` (boolean): Segment tables only. Available from Archicad 29.
- `minimumSegmentationLength` (number): Segment tables only; the maximum is kept when not given. Available from Archicad 29.
- `maximumSegmentationLength` (number): Segment tables only; the minimum is kept when not given. Available from Archicad 29.
- `rows` (array of MEPPreferenceRowChange): The rows to change or delete, each at most once. All indices refer to the table before this call.
- `newRows` (array of object): Rows to add to a rectangular duct or cable carrier segment table, after the other changes. Adding rows to the other tables is not supported yet.
  - `value` (number, required)
  - `description` (string)

### MEPComponentType

string ("Terminal", "Accessory", "Equipment", "Fitting")

### LibPartUnId

object
- `guid` (Guid, required)

### MEPPreferenceRow

object
- `index` (MEPPreferenceRowIndex)
- `referenceId` (integer, required)
- `diameter` (number, required)
- `wallThickness` (number)
- `description` (string)
- `isValid` (boolean): Whether the row is valid.

### MEPElement

object
- `elementId` (ElementId, required)
- `type` (MEPElementType, required): The type of the MEP element.
- `domain` (string, required): The MEP domain of the element. Empty for domain-independent elements (e.g. Equipment).
- `localizedTypeName` (string): The type name of the element in the language of Archicad. Only returned by Archicad 28.

### MEPDistributionSystem

object
- `domain` (MEPDomainOrUnknown, required)
- `mepSystemId` (AttributeId)
- `elements` (Elements, required)
- `physicalSystemIds` (array of MEPPhysicalSystemId): The physical systems of the distribution system. From Archicad 29; missing when Archicad could not tell.
- `tree` (array of MEPDistributionSystemTreeNode): The elements of the system from its root element on, in the order Archicad traverses them. Only returned when includeTree is true, and missing when Archicad could not traverse the system.

### MEPDistributionSystemTreeNode

object: An element of a distribution system tree.
- `elementId` (ElementId, required)
- `depth` (integer, required): The number of steps from the root element; 0 for the root element.
- `previousElementId` (ElementId): The element before this one on the way from the root element. Missing for the root element.
- `connectedPortIdOfPreviousElement` (string): The port of the previous element this element is connected to (see GetMEPPorts). Missing when Archicad gives none.
- `connectedPortIdOfThisElement` (string): The port of this element that is connected to the previous element (see GetMEPPorts). Missing when Archicad gives none.
- `nextElements` (Elements, required): The elements after this one, away from the root element.

### MEPPreferenceTable

object
- `guid` (string, required)
- `name` (string)
- `isEditable` (boolean): Whether the table can be edited.
- `useIndividualSegmentLengths` (boolean): Whether the table uses individual segmentation lengths. Available from Archicad 29.
- `minimumSegmentationLength` (number): Available from Archicad 29.
- `maximumSegmentationLength` (number): Available from Archicad 29.
- `rows` (array of MEPPreferenceRow, required)

### MEPValuePreferenceTable

object: A rectangular duct or cable carrier segment preference table: a list of sizes.
- `guid` (string, required)
- `name` (string)
- `isEditable` (boolean): Whether the table can be edited.
- `useIndividualSegmentLengths` (boolean): Whether the table uses individual segmentation lengths. Available from Archicad 29.
- `minimumSegmentationLength` (number): Available from Archicad 29.
- `maximumSegmentationLength` (number): Available from Archicad 29.
- `rows` (array of object, required)
  - `index` (MEPPreferenceRowIndex)
  - `value` (number, required): The size of the row.
  - `description` (string)

### MEPOrientation

object: The orientation of an MEP element, given by a direction and a rotation vector.
- `direction` (Coordinate3D, required): The direction vector.
- `rotation` (Coordinate3D, required): The rotation vector.

### ElectricalLoads

object: An electrical load in total and per phase, as Archicad calculates it.
- `total` (number, required)
- `phaseA` (number, required)
- `phaseB` (number, required)
- `phaseC` (number, required)

### ElectricalPanelDetails

object: The details of an electrical panel (distribution board).
- `elementId` (ElementId, required)
- `panelName` (string, required)
- `circuitNamePrefix` (string, required): The prefix of the names of the circuits of the panel.
- `circuitIdStyle` (integer, required): The index of the style of the circuit ids.
- `circuits` (Elements, required): The circuits owned by the panel.
- `parentCircuitId` (ElementId): The circuit the panel is connected to. Missing when the panel is not connected to a circuit.
- `anchorPoint` (Coordinate3D, required): The anchor point of the element.
- `orientation` (MEPOrientation, required)
- `rotation` (number, required): The base rotation of the element in radians.
- `isReflected` (boolean, required): The element is mirrored.
- `libraryPartId` (LibPartUnId, required): The library part of the element.
- `xSize` (number, required): The size of the element along its local x axis.
- `ySize` (number, required): The size of the element along its local y axis.
- `connectedLoad` (ElectricalLoads, required)
- `demandLoad` (ElectricalLoads, required)

### ElectricalPanelDetailsOrError

ElectricalPanelDetails or ErrorItem: The details of an electrical panel or an error.

### ElectricalCircuitDetails

object: The details of an electrical circuit.
- `elementId` (ElementId, required)
- `name` (string, required): The name of the circuit, including the circuit name prefix of its panel.
- `description` (string, required)
- `ownerPanelId` (ElementId, required): The panel that owns the circuit.
- `childDevices` (Elements, required): The electrical devices connected to the circuit.
- `childPanels` (Elements, required): The electrical panels connected to the circuit.
- `voltage` (number, required)
- `phases` (string, required): The used phases, as Archicad displays them.
- `isPhaseAUsed` (boolean, required)
- `isPhaseBUsed` (boolean, required)

### MEPElementDetails

object
- `elementId` (ElementId, required)
- `type` (MEPElementType, required)
- `domain` (string, required): The MEP domain (Ventilation, Piping or CableCarrier), empty if the element has none.
- `insulationThickness` (number): The insulation thickness. RigidSegment, Elbow, Branch and Transition.
- `routingSegmentId` (ElementId): The routing segment the rigid segment belongs to (see GetMEPRoutingElements). RigidSegment.
- `routingNodeId` (ElementId): The routing node the elbow or transition belongs to (see GetMEPRoutingElements). Elbow and Transition.
- `controlPoints` (array of Coordinate3D): The control points of the flexible segment. FlexibleSegment.
- `polyline` (MEPFlexibleSegmentPolyline): The line and spline parts of the flexible segment, when Archicad gives them (a flexible segment placed as a polyline, see CreateMEPFlexibleSegments). FlexibleSegment.
- `factorRadius` (number): The radius factor of the elbow (Elbow::GetFactorRadius). Elbow, from Archicad 29.
- `preferenceTableId` (Guid): The guid of the elbow or transition preference table (see GetMEPPreferenceTables). Elbow and Transition, from Archicad 29.
- `branchAngle` (number): The angle of the branch, as returned by Branch::GetBranchAngle. Branch.
- `branchLength` (number): The length of the branch. Branch.
- `offsetY` (number): The Y offset of the transition (Transition::GetOffsetY). Transition.
- `offsetZ` (number): The Z offset of the transition (Transition::GetOffsetZ). Transition.
- `widerPortId` (Guid): The port at the wider end of the transition (see GetMEPPorts). Transition.
- `narrowerPortId` (Guid): The port at the narrower end of the transition (see GetMEPPorts). Transition.
- `isControlledByPreference` (boolean): Whether the transition is controlled by its preference table. Transition, from Archicad 29.
- `width` (number): The width of the flexible segment (FlexibleSegment::GetWidth), as ModifyMEPElements writes it. FlexibleSegment.
- `height` (number): The height of the flexible segment (FlexibleSegment::GetHeight), as ModifyMEPElements writes it. FlexibleSegment.
- `anchorPoint` (Coordinate3D): The anchor point, as ModifyMEPElements writes it. The elements ModifyMEPElements can place: Terminal, Accessory, Equipment, Fitting, FlexibleSegment and the other modifiable MEP elements.
- `orientation` (MEPOrientation): The orientation, as ModifyMEPElements writes it. Present with anchorPoint.
- `libraryPartId` (LibPartUnId): The library part the element uses (its main guid), as ModifyMEPElements writes it. Present with anchorPoint.
- `xSize` (number): The size of the library part along the element's local x axis in meters, as ModifyMEPElements writes it. Present with anchorPoint, from Archicad 30.
- `ySize` (number): The size of the library part along the element's local y axis in meters, as ModifyMEPElements writes it. Present with anchorPoint, from Archicad 30.

### MEPRoutingElementData

object
- `domain` (MEPDomain, required)
- `nodeCoordinates` (array of Coordinate3D, required): The corner points of the route polyline.
- `crossSectionWidth` (number): Optional cross section width applied to all segments.
- `crossSectionHeight` (number): Optional cross section height applied to all segments.
- `crossSectionShape` (MEPCrossSectionShape): Optional; applied to all segments.
- `crossSectionReferenceId` (integer): Optional cross section reference id of the segment preference table (used for circular cross sections). Resolved against preferenceTableId if given, otherwise against the table of the current routing tool default.
- `preferenceTableId` (Guid): Optional guid of the segment preference table (see GetMEPPreferenceTables) applied to all segments. Not applicable to the CableCarrier domain.
- `mepSystemId` (AttributeId): Optional MEP system attribute.
- `layerIndex` (integer): Optional layer attribute index of the routing element and all its parts (routing segments, rigid segments, elbows and transitions). Only a positive index takes effect; otherwise the routing tool default layer is used. A layer that does not exist or is locked gives an error for the item, and nothing is placed.
- `floorIndex` (integer): Optional home story index (as returned by GetStories) of the routing element and all its parts. The node coordinates stay absolute: the route is placed at them, then moved to this home story. Without it, Archicad picks the home story, which follows the active story. A story that does not exist gives an error for the item, and nothing is placed.
- `defaults` (object): Optional changes to the routing tool default of the domain before the route is placed. Only what is placed changes, not the routing tool's settings. A value that cannot be set gives an error for the item, and nothing is placed.
  - `routingNode` (object): The routing node default: the elbows and transitions placed at the nodes of the route. Available from Archicad 29.

### MEPPortCreationData

object
- `portIndex` (integer, required): Zero-based index of the port in the library part.
- `mepSystemId` (AttributeId): The MEP system of the port.
- `shape` (MEPCrossSectionShape): The shape of the port.
- `width` (number): The width of the port.
- `height` (number): The height of a ventilation or cable carrier port.
- `diameter` (number): The diameter of a piping port.

### MEPElementData

object
- `type` (MEPComponentType, required)
- `domain` (MEPDomain): Required for all types except Equipment. For Equipment it only selects the ports that mepSystemId is applied to.
- `position` (Coordinate3D, required)
- `libraryPartId` (LibPartUnId): Optional library part to place instead of the one in the tool's settings, as listed by GetAvailableLibraryParts. Its ports replace the default ones, so 'ports' refers to the ports of this library part. Its ports keep the MEP system of the library part, which may be none, so give 'mepSystemId' with it to connect it. If it is not found, the item fails and nothing is placed.
- `xSize` (number): Optional size along the local x axis in meters. Available from Archicad 30. Some library parts calculate their own size and keep it.
- `ySize` (number): Optional size along the local y axis in meters. Available from Archicad 30. Some library parts calculate their own size and keep it.
- `mepSystemId` (AttributeId): Optional MEP system of the ports of the element's domain (of every port when an Equipment item has no domain). The 'mepSystemId' of an entry of 'ports' overrides it for that port.
- `ports` (array of MEPPortCreationData): Optional changes to single ports of the element before it is placed. The values are in meters.
- `orientationDirection` (Coordinate3D): Optional direction vector of the orientation. Defaults to (1, 0, 0).
- `orientationRotation` (Coordinate3D): Optional rotation vector of the orientation. Defaults to (0, 1, 0).
- `floorIndex` (integer): Optional home story index (as returned by GetStories). The position stays absolute: the element is placed at it, then moved to this home story. Without it, Archicad picks the home story, which follows the active story. A story that does not exist gives an error for the item, and nothing is placed.
- `defaults` (object): Optional changes to the tool default before the element is placed. Only what is placed changes, not the tool's settings. A value that cannot be set gives an error for the item, and nothing is placed.
  - `insulationThickness` (number): The insulation thickness in meters.
  - `removeInsulation` (boolean): If true, the element is placed without insulation. Cannot be combined with insulationThickness.

### MEPRoutingElementModificationData

object
- `elementId` (ElementId, required)
- `mepSystemId` (AttributeId)
- `crossSectionWidth` (number): New cross section width applied to all segments.
- `crossSectionHeight` (number): New cross section height applied to all segments.
- `crossSectionShape` (MEPCrossSectionShape): The new shape is applied to all segments.
- `crossSectionReferenceId` (integer): New cross section reference id of the segment preference table applied to all segments (used for circular cross sections). Resolved against preferenceTableId if given, otherwise against the table the segments already use.
- `preferenceTableId` (Guid): New segment preference table (guid as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables) applied to all segments. Not applicable to the CableCarrier domain.
- `branchPreferenceTableId` (Guid): New branch preference table (guid as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables) of the routing element.
- `anchor` (MEPRoutingAnchor): Applied to all segments of the routing element.
- `referenceLineOffsetX` (number): New horizontal offset of the reference line from the anchor point, applied to all segments.
- `referenceLineOffsetY` (number): New vertical offset of the reference line from the anchor point, applied to all segments.
- `wallThickness` (number): New wall thickness applied to all segments.
- `flangeSize` (number): New flange size applied to all segments. Needs the Flanged connection style, which can be set in the same call.
- `insulationThickness` (number): New insulation thickness of the route, as Insulation in its settings: applied to the rigid segments of all segments and to the elbows (bends in Archicad 28) and transitions at all nodes. 0 removes the insulation. Not applicable to the CableCarrier domain.
- `connectionStyle` (MEPConnectionStyle): New connection style applied to all segments.
- `preferredTransitionPlacement` (MEPPreferredTransitionPlacement): New preferred transition placement applied to all nodes.
- `cutPlanePosition` (MEPCutPlanePosition): New cut plane position of the routing element. Available from Archicad 29.
- `floorPlanDisplayOption` (MEPFloorPlanDisplayOption): New floor plan display option of the routing element. Available from Archicad 29.
- `showProjection` (MEPShowProjection): New show projection setting of the routing element. Available from Archicad 29.
- `onStoryVisibility` (MEPOnStoryVisibility): New on-story visibility of the routing element. Available from Archicad 29.
- `nodePositions` (array of Coordinate3D): New positions of the routing nodes. The size must match the number of nodes of the route. A first or last node that is connected to a tee (Branch) must keep its position (within 1 mm): moving a route end away from its tee can crash Archicad, and no command moves a tee, so such an item is refused and nothing of it is changed. GetMEPRoutingElements reads them back with the same key.

### MEPPortModificationData

object
- `portId` (Guid, required): The port to modify, as returned by GetMEPPorts.
- `shape` (MEPCrossSectionShape): New shape of the port.
- `width` (number): New width of the port (the connection size of a terminal, accessory, equipment or fitting), in meters. The ports of routes and branches take their size from the route instead.
- `height` (number): New height of a ventilation or cable carrier port, in meters. A piping port's size is its 'outerDiameter'.
- `connectionStyle` (MEPConnectionStyle): New connection style of the port. Available from Archicad 30.
- `flowDirection` (MEPFlowDirection): New flow direction of a piping or ventilation port.
- `outerDiameter` (number): New outer diameter of a piping port.
- `nominalSize` (string): New nominal size of a piping port. Available from Archicad 30.

### MEPConnectionData

object
- `routingElementId` (ElementId, required): The routing element to connect to. When connecting two routes, the first or last node of the 'connectToId' route must lie exactly on this route (on its centerline, not within a tolerance). For a tee, this is the main route, which is split and gets the branch element.
- `connectToId` (ElementId, required): The MEP element or routing element connected to 'routingElementId'. For a tee, this is the branch route, whose first or last node lies on the main route. Two routes must have the same domain and MEP system; an MEP element's port must match the route in domain and MEP system, lie on its first or last node and point in the opposite direction.

### MEPFlexibleSegmentCreationData

object
- `domain` (MEPDomain, required)
- `controlPoints` (array of Coordinate3D): The control points of the flexible segment, from its beginning to its end. Give either 'controlPoints' or 'polyline'.
- `startOrientation` (MEPOrientation): Optional orientation at the beginning, with 'controlPoints'. Defaults to the direction from the first control point to the second one, with a horizontal rotation vector perpendicular to it.
- `endOrientation` (MEPOrientation): Optional orientation at the end, with 'controlPoints'. Defaults to the direction from the last but one control point to the last one, with a horizontal rotation vector perpendicular to it.
- `polyline` (MEPFlexibleSegmentPolyline): The flexible segment as alternating line and spline parts that connect at their ends, instead of 'controlPoints'. Archicad places polyline flexible segments in the Piping domain only.
- `startDirection` (Coordinate3D): Optional direction vector at the beginning, with 'polyline'. Only when the first part is a spline.
- `endDirection` (Coordinate3D): Optional direction vector at the end, with 'polyline'. Only when the last part is a spline.

### MEPTakeOffCreationData

object
- `domain` (MEPDomain): Optional domain of the Take-Off tool whose settings are used. Defaults to the domain of the segment's routing element. Archicad currently only has Ventilation take-offs.
- `segmentId` (ElementId, required): The routing segment to place the take-off on (the elementId of an item of 'segments' returned by GetMEPRoutingElements).
- `distanceFromBeginning` (number, required): The distance of the take-off from the beginning of the segment, in meters. Must not be negative or more than the length of the segment.
- `rotationAroundMainAxis` (number): Optional rotation of the take-off around the axis of the segment, in radians. Archicad places take-offs only at quarter turns, so it must be a multiple of pi/2 (negative values and full turns are allowed). Defaults to 0, which places the take-off facing left relative to the segment's direction; pi/2 faces up, pi faces right, 3*pi/2 (or -pi/2) faces down.
- `length` (number): Optional length of the take-off in meters, set after placing it; must be positive. The length of the Take-Off tool when not given.
- `defaults` (object): Optional changes to the settings of the Take-Off tool before the take-off is placed. Only what is placed changes, not the tool's settings. A value that cannot be set gives an error for the item, and nothing is placed. The insulation thickness of a take-off cannot be set (Archicad stops with a fatal error).
  - `removeInsulation` (boolean): If true, the take-off is placed without insulation.

### MEPElementModificationData

object
- `elementId` (ElementId, required)
- `anchorPoint` (Coordinate3D): The new anchor point of a terminal, accessory, equipment, fitting or flexible segment.
- `orientation` (MEPOrientation): The new orientation of a terminal, accessory, equipment, fitting or flexible segment.
- `libraryPartId` (LibPartUnId): The library part a terminal, accessory, equipment or fitting uses, as listed by GetAvailableLibraryParts. If it is not found, the element keeps its library part and the item fails.
- `controlPoints` (array of Coordinate3D): The new control points of a flexible segment, from its beginning to its end. Not together with 'polyline'.
- `polyline` (MEPFlexibleSegmentPolyline): The new geometry of a Piping flexible segment as alternating line and spline parts that connect at their ends. Not together with 'controlPoints'. Available from Archicad 28.
- `width` (number): The new width of a flexible segment. It is written before height: on Archicad 29 a Ventilation flexible duct of the template then read the height given in the same item as its width too (probably a round duct, whose width and height are one diameter), so give such a duct one of them.
- `height` (number): The new height of a flexible segment, written after width.
- `xSize` (number): The new size of a terminal, accessory, equipment or fitting along its local x axis, in meters. Some library parts calculate their own size and keep it, then the item fails after its other changes were made. The size of its connections is set with ModifyMEPPorts. Available from Archicad 30.
- `ySize` (number): The new size of a terminal, accessory, equipment or fitting along its local y axis, in meters. Some library parts calculate their own size and keep it, then the item fails after its other changes were made. Available from Archicad 30.

object: Transition parameters. preferenceTableId is given from Archicad 29.

- `offsetY` (number)
- `offsetZ` (number)
- `preferenceTableId` (Guid)

### MEPRoutingNodeParameters

object: The routing node default parameters of a routing element (RoutingElement::GetRoutingNodeDefaultParameters). The elbow is given from Archicad 29.

- `elbow` (MEPElbowParameters)
- `transition` (MEPTransitionParameters)

object: The rigid segment default parameters of a routing segment (RoutingSegment::GetRigidSegmentDefaultParameters). Archicad 28 only.
